priorStories.headline: Two shootings in South Africa kill 27
priorStories.body:
Two separate shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town killed 27 people, and South African police were searching for suspects Sunday.

One attack at a tavern in Wedela township killed 17 people and injured 15 on Saturday evening. Authorities were investigating whether an illegal-mining turf dispute was behind one shooting and a business rivalry was behind the other.

candidates.summary: Ukraine's military struck Russian oil facilities in the Krasnodar region, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday. The Reuters report did not identify the facilities or provide an independent damage assessment.
candidates.title: Ukraine says it struck oil facilities in Russia's Krasnodar region

candidates.summary: China's Commerce Ministry confirmed that a two-month extension of the country's trade truce with the United States will run through January 10. The ministry said the extension gives both sides time to assess implementation of their arrangement and continue economic and trade discussions.
candidates.title: China confirms extension of US trade truce through January 10

candidates.summary: Preliminary Kpler data released Monday showed September crude exports from major Middle Eastern producers rising to 12.8 million barrels per day, the highest level since the Iran war began in February. Saudi Arabia was on track to export about 5.4 million barrels per day, up from 2.446 million in August, though total regional exports remained below February levels.
candidates.title: Middle East crude exports rebound in September

candidates.summary: South Korea's military said preliminary findings indicated that blasts in the Demilitarized Zone on September 21 were highly likely caused by a North Korean mine. Three South Korean soldiers were injured, two seriously. The military said it would hold North Korea accountable and take corresponding measures if the finding is confirmed.
candidates.title: South Korea says North Korean mine likely caused DMZ blast

candidates.summary: Qatari mediators were expected to hold separate talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and the United States on Monday or Tuesday, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters. The discussions were expected to concern an amended version of Iran's proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming broader negotiations.
candidates.title: Qatari mediators plan separate US-Iran talks

candidates.summary: At least 33 people were killed and 36 injured in a Myanmar military airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw, Rakhine state, according to the Arakan Army and a local aid worker cited by Reuters. Reuters attributed the attack to the military but did not report an immediate response from the junta.
candidates.title: Airstrike reportedly kills at least 33 in Myanmar's Rakhine state

candidates.summary: Thailand's Constitutional Court dismissed a petition challenging the legality of the February general election. The court ruled that identifying codes printed on ballot papers did not violate voter secrecy. The election was won by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's Bhumjaithai Party.
candidates.title: Thai court rejects challenge to 2026 general election

candidates.summary: South Korea's Foreign Ministry summoned Ukraine's acting ambassador to protest Kyiv's disclosure that captured North Korean soldiers had been transferred to South Korea. Seoul said the disclosure breached an agreement to keep the transfer confidential and requested an official explanation and apology.
candidates.title: South Korea summons Ukrainian envoy over POW-transfer disclosure

candidates.summary: China's Commerce Ministry confirmed that a two-month extension of the country's trade truce with the United States will run through January 10. The two countries also agreed to reduce tariffs on $60 billion of bilateral trade, split evenly between lists of U.S. and Chinese goods, although Reuters reported no timetable for implementing the reductions.
candidates.title: China confirms US trade-truce extension and tariff-cut agreement

candidates.summary: Thirteen people were killed in a fire at a pyrotechnics factory in Kubrinsk in Russia's Yaroslavl region, TASS reported, citing emergency services. The fire engulfed two buildings, and authorities opened a criminal investigation into alleged violations of industrial-safety regulations.
candidates.title: Fire at Russian pyrotechnics factory kills 13

candidates.summary: A court in Rome convicted three Egyptian security officials of involvement in the 2016 kidnapping and killing of Italian doctoral researcher Giulio Regeni and sentenced each to 10 years in prison. A fourth defendant was acquitted. The defendants were tried in absentia.
candidates.title: Italian court convicts three Egyptian officials in Giulio Regeni case

candidates.summary: Russian draft budget documents reviewed by Reuters call for 17.1 trillion roubles in defense spending in 2027, about 27% above the amount previously budgeted. The documents also raise the estimated 2026 budget deficit to 3.2% of gross domestic product. The draft had not yet been submitted to parliament, which was expected by October 1.
candidates.title: Russian draft budget raises planned 2027 defense spending

candidates.summary: The U.S. Transportation Department finalized vehicle fuel-economy standards requiring a fleetwide average of 34.9 miles per gallon by 2031, down from the prior 50.4-mpg requirement. Department estimates said the rule would lower manufacturers' compliance costs but increase lifetime fuel costs and gasoline consumption compared with the superseded standards.
candidates.title: US finalizes lower vehicle fuel-economy standards

candidates.summary: U.S. District Judge Amir Ali blocked the Trump administration from withholding portions of federal counterterrorism grants unless state and local governments adopted administration-backed election procedures. The judge ruled that Congress had not authorized the grant programs to be conditioned on those election-administration changes.
candidates.title: US judge blocks election conditions on counterterrorism grants

candidates.summary: Pennsylvania reported 68 additional measles infections since September 23, bringing the state's outbreak total to 903, according to state health department data. Hospitalizations rose to 176 from 164, with Lancaster County remaining the state's hardest-hit area.
candidates.title: Pennsylvania measles outbreak exceeds 900 cases

candidates.summary: India announced that Trade Minister Piyush Goyal would visit the United States from September 29 through October 5 for talks intended to advance a bilateral trade agreement and finalize an interim deal. The government said he would also attend a G20 trade ministers' meeting in Wisconsin.
candidates.title: India announces US visit for trade-deal negotiations
